prompt: The app feels slow, so an engineer starts rewriting the sorting code. A teammate asks whether anyone has profiled it.
tells: asks whether anyone has profiled it
why: Find the real bottleneck before optimizing.
trap: It's not about proving a fix works; it's finding where time goes.

prompt: An engineer adds a cache to speed up a page. Afterwards the page is just as slow; a profiler shows 90% of the time is a single image download.
tells: a profiler shows 90% of the time is a single image download
why: Optimizing a guess wasted the effort.
trap: The cache wasn't speculative; it was aimed at the wrong place.

prompt: Before tuning the API, the team records its current p99 latency so they can tell whether changes help.
trap: It's not testing correctness; it's measuring speed.

prompt: In code review, someone asks to replace a loop with a 'faster' trick. The function runs once a day on 50 items.
tells: runs once a day on 50 items
why: Optimize what matters by the numbers.
trap: Close to YAGNI, but the cue is speed without evidence.

prompt: In a system design interview, the candidate estimates reads per second and storage per year before deciding whether a cache is needed.
tells: estimates reads per second and storage per year before deciding whether a cache is needed
why: Numbers decide the optimization, not instinct.
trap: Requirements are known; this is estimating load before optimizing.

prompt: Instead of adding indexes everywhere, the engineer reads the slow-query log and the query plan to find the one query that needs one.
tells: reads the slow-query log and the query plan
why: Data points to the real fix.
trap: Nothing is down; it's tuning by evidence.
